transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate you taking the time. 

Um... well, I'm probably making a bigger deal out of this than it is, but I've just been having a little trouble at work lately. I guess what finally scared me into coming in—and I hope it's okay that I'm here for this—is that I just keep making these... well, kind of dumb technical mistakes. Things I absolutely know better than to make. 

Like, um, labeling camera cards wrong on set, or missing a timecode note. Or I'll export a client cut with the wrong lower-third graphic on it, even after I swear I’ve already checked it. It's just a bit embarrassing, honestly, because I really do try to be careful and I'm usually good at my job. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm not wasting your time with all this.
Have you had problems with inattention or making careless mistakes like this since you were a child?

Um... well, I guess looking back... yeah, maybe a little? I mean, I was always just a really... enthusiastic kid, I guess you could say. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a troublemaker, because I really did always want to be good! 

But, um, even back in elementary school, my teachers actually had to move my desk around a lot. I just... I had so much energy, so I was always sort of popping out of my seat, or, um, blurting out the answers because I just got so excited to participate. And I guess I would end up bothering my classmates a bit, but I promise I never meant to! I'd just do it before I even realized what I was doing, and then I'd feel awful when the teacher had to correct me. 

Is... is that the kind of thing you mean? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.
Have these work mistakes started after a specific stressful or traumatic event recently?

Um... no, definitely nothing traumatic or anything like that! I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I know I'm very lucky to have my job. But... I guess it has been happening at this sort of, well, disruptive level for about two years and two months now? 

There wasn't a trauma, but there was a... a company readjustment right around then. It ended up changing how all my shoots and my edit reviews are run. It's not a bad thing, it's just a different workflow, and I guess I just haven't adapted quite as perfectly as I should have. I really do try my absolute best to stay on top of the new system, but since they made that change, I've just been struggling a bit more to keep everything straight without making those little errors. 

Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of timeline you were looking for!
Over the past two years, have you felt depressed or down most days?

Oh, um, no, definitely not! I mean, I think I have normal off days just like anyone else, but I certainly wouldn't say I've felt depressed or down most days. 

I really try to stay positive, you know? I have a great life and I'm so lucky to do what I do, so I'd feel just awful complaining about being sad when I have so much to be grateful for. It's really just the frustration with myself when I make those silly mistakes at work, not a... a depression thing. 

Is... is that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and not confusing things.
Do you find yourself doing repetitive rituals or mental checking to prevent mistakes or something bad from happening?

Oh, gosh, no... nothing like that! I mean, obviously, as an editor, I do try to look over my cuts and my footage to catch those little careless errors I mentioned, just because I really want to do a good job for my team. But it's definitely not a... a repetitive ritual, and I'm not doing it because I think something terrible is going to happen. It's really just normal work stuff, I promise! I don't have any rigid routines or anything like that. 

I hope I'm not misunderstanding the question... is that what you were asking about?
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about different things most days?

Oh, um, no, I really wouldn't say I'm a worrier! I mean, I have normal, everyday concerns, of course—like making sure my cuts are turned in on time or hoping the director is happy with my work—but... I definitely don't spend a lot of time worrying about different things every day. 

I really try to just take things as they come and stay upbeat. I wouldn't want to be the kind of person who's constantly stressing out and bringing everyone else down, you know? So, no, I don't think I struggle with worrying. 

Is that... does that answer what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most accurate picture!
